title: SVG & Icon Accessibility ✨
description: Make scalable vector graphics and icon systems perceivable and navigable for all users.

slides.title: SVG: More Than Just an Image 🎨
slides.content:
Inline SVGs can contain real text, shapes, and interactivity. Accessibility requires:

* Use `<title>` and `<desc>` inside the SVG for a short name and longer description.
* Add `aria-labelledby` on the `<svg>` element pointing to the `<title>` (and optionally `<desc>`).
* For decorative SVGs, add `aria-hidden="true"` and omit `<title>`.
* Ensure text inside SVG is real text, not outlines (so screen readers can access it).

slides.title: Accessible Inline SVG
slides.codeSnippet:
<svg aria-labelledby="graph-title graph-desc" role="img">
  <title id="graph-title">Revenue Growth</title>
  <desc id="graph-desc">A bar chart showing revenue increase from 2020 to 2025.</desc>
  <!-- chart shapes -->
</svg>

quizData.question: What role should an informative inline SVG have?
quizData.explanation: `role='img'` ensures it is treated as a single image by assistive tech.

slides.title: Icon Systems & Sprites 🧩
slides.content:
Icons are often used from sprite sheets or via `<svg><use>`. Accessibility rules:

* **Decorative icons** (next to a text label) – `aria-hidden="true"`.
* **Standalone icon buttons** (e.g., menu toggle with no text) – provide an accessible name using `aria-label` on the button, not the SVG.
* **Linked icons** – wrap the SVG in an `<a>` and give the link an accessible name (via `aria-label` or visible text).

Example: `<button aria-label="Open menu"><svg aria-hidden="true">...</svg></button>`

quizData.question: A close button contains only an 'X' SVG icon. How do you make it accessible?
quizData.explanation: The button element should carry the accessible name; the SVG should be hidden from assistive tech (`aria-hidden='true'`).

slides.title: Interactive SVGs & Focus 🖱️
slides.content:
If your SVG contains clickable elements (like a map), each interactive part must:

* Be focusable (`tabindex="0"`).
* Have a role (e.g., `role="link"` or `role="button"`).
* Have an accessible name (`aria-label`).
* Be reachable and operable with the keyboard.

Consider offering a text‑based alternative (e.g., a list of locations).
